chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)”?

options.label: A
options.text: An NMR technique recording the distinct chemical shifts of carbon-13 nuclei across an organic carbon framework.

options.label: B
options.text: A spectroscopic method detecting the absorption of radiofrequency radiation by atomic nuclei with nonzero spin placed in an external magnetic field.

options.label: C
options.text: The magnetic interaction strength between coupled nuclei, measured in Hertz (Hz), which is independent of the external magnetic field strength.

options.label: D
options.text: A distortionless enhancement by polarization transfer technique in 13C NMR that differentiates CH3, CH2, CH, and quaternary carbon signals.

questions.correct_answer: A spectroscopic method detecting the absorption of radiofrequency radiation by atomic nuclei with nonzero spin placed in an external magnetic field.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is: A spectroscopic method detecting the absorption of radiofrequency radiation by atomic nuclei with nonzero spin placed in an external magnetic field.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which organic chemistry term best matches this description? The position of an NMR absorption resonance relative to a reference standard (tetramethylsilane, TMS), measured in parts per million (ppm).

options.label: A
options.text: coupling constant (J)

options.label: B
options.text: chemical shift

options.label: C
options.text: DEPT NMR

options.label: D
options.text: spin–spin splitting

questions.correct_answer: chemical shift
questions.explanation: The best match is chemical shift: The position of an NMR absorption resonance relative to a reference standard (tetramethylsilane, TMS), measured in parts per million (ppm).

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “shielding”?

options.label: A
options.text: An NMR technique recording the distinct chemical shifts of carbon-13 nuclei across an organic carbon framework.

options.label: B
options.text: The reduction of the effective magnetic field experienced by a nucleus due to electron density circulating around it, shifting the resonance upfield.

options.label: C
options.text: The splitting of an NMR signal into multiple peaks caused by the magnetic influence of neighboring, non-equivalent nuclei.

options.label: D
options.text: A spectroscopic method detecting the absorption of radiofrequency radiation by atomic nuclei with nonzero spin placed in an external magnetic field.

questions.correct_answer: The reduction of the effective magnetic field experienced by a nucleus due to electron density circulating around it, shifting the resonance upfield.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of shielding is: The reduction of the effective magnetic field experienced by a nucleus due to electron density circulating around it, shifting the resonance upfield.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which organic chemistry term best matches this description? The decrease in local electron density surrounding a nucleus caused by electronegative atoms or magnetic anisotropy, shifting the resonance downfield.

options.label: A
options.text: DEPT NMR

options.label: B
options.text: shielding

options.label: C
options.text: deshielding

options.label: D
options.text: nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)
